props.heading: Bringing out the best in every child
props.subheading: Moriah School is an English-medium school for Pre-KG to Class 10, where every child is known, valued and equipped to grow into a capable, compassionate adult.

props.heading: An education that brings out each child's best
props.html:
Since 1999, Moriah School has served students from pre-kindergarten through Class 10 in Guntur. Our school was founded on a simple conviction: every child deserves an education that nurtures character, curiosity and competence — not just exam scores.

Our students are known and valued. They are equipped not only for academic success, but to grow into capable, compassionate adults who are committed to serving their neighbours.

props.heading: Why families choose Moriah
props.intro: A safe, joyful school where children learn deeply and grow in confidence.

items.title: Every child known
items.text: Caring teachers who know each student by name, encourage them and keep families closely involved.

items.title: Strong English foundation
items.text: An English-medium school with a dedicated English language programme supported by mentors.

items.title: Science & discovery
items.text: Practical science, STEM activities and early robotics spark curiosity and problem solving.

items.title: Arts, dance & sport
items.text: Dance, art and games build confidence, teamwork and joy alongside academics.

items.title: Open to all
items.text: Sliding-scale fees and financial aid so that no child is turned away for lack of means.

props.heading: Founded by a teacher, for the children who need it most
props.html:
In 1999, Mrs. Devakaruna Dasari opened Moriah School so that children from poor families in Guntur could receive a quality education. Alongside the school, Moriah Home has cared for children without parents since 1985.

Today her family, the Bible Faith Lutheran Church of India and our teachers carry her vision forward.

props.heading: Improving lives through education
props.subheading: Moriah School has given children from Guntur's working families a quality education for more than 25 years.

props.heading: A school for every child
props.html:
Moriah School is a government-recognised, private English-medium school for students from Pre-Kindergarten to Class 10 in Guntur, Andhra Pradesh. Our teachers prepare every student for the Class 10 board examinations and for the next step to college.

The school was founded so that children from families with limited means could receive a quality education. For many of our students, they are the first in their family to go to school — and each one of them helps break the cycle of missed education.

Moriah is open to children of every faith and background. Fees follow a sliding scale based on what each family can afford, and financial aid is available for qualified students.

props.heading: A teacher's dream, begun in 1999
props.html:
Moriah School was founded in 1999 by the late Mrs. Devakaruna Dasari. As a girl in her village, she received her own education at a small private school much like Moriah — and she never forgot what it opened up for her.

Her vision was simple: children from poor families deserve the same quality education, one that equips them to serve their neighbours. She led the school and Moriah Home until her passing in 2011.

props.heading: A safe and nurturing home
props.html:
Since 1985, Moriah Home has given children who have lost one or both parents — or who need reliable care and a safe place to live — a stable, loving home. Today it cares full-time for more than 20 children, and over the years it has been home to hundreds.

Every child at Moriah Home studies at Moriah School, so home and school work hand in hand.

props.heading: Who looks after Moriah
props.intro: Moriah School and Moriah Home are guided by a church, a local leadership team and a family of trustees.

items.title: Bible Faith Lutheran Church of India
items.text: Founded in 1978 by Rev. Dasari Bhushana Rao, the church (BFLC India) is responsible for the direction and care of Moriah Home.

items.title: Leadership in Guntur
items.text: Bishop G. Shalem Raju oversees the day-to-day running of both the school and the home, with Mrs. Swarupa and a team of more than 20 staff.

items.title: The Dasari family trustees
items.text: The founders' three children — David, Paul and Esther — serve as trustees, making sure Moriah's mission continues.

props.html:
Our history

Over the years Moriah has educated hundreds of students, with enrolment ranging from a few dozen to more than 400. Our location, uniform and staff have changed over time, but our commitment to quality education for every child has not. Through the COVID pandemic and difficult years, the school has continued its mission quietly and faithfully.

Many Moriah students have gone on to become teachers, nurses, software engineers, optometrists, pastors and professors — and each graduate carries Mrs. Dasari's vision forward.

props.heading: Welcome to Moriah School
props.html:
Dear parents and friends,

At Moriah, we believe that education is about far more than marks. It is about helping every child discover their gifts, grow in character and gain the confidence to make a difference in the world.

Our teachers know each student personally. We combine strong foundations in English, mathematics and science with art, dance, games and plenty of hands-on learning — because children learn best when they are curious, safe and happy.

Thank you for considering Moriah for your child. Our doors are always open: please visit us, meet our teachers and see our classrooms for yourself.

The Principal
Moriah School, Guntur

items.title: Vision
items.text: That every child — whatever their background — receives an education that brings out his or her best and nurtures character, curiosity and competence.

items.title: Mission
items.text: To provide a learning environment in which students are known and valued, and equipped not only for academic success but to grow into capable, compassionate adults committed to serving their neighbours.

items.text: Every child is known, valued and safe.

items.title: Service

props.heading: Strong foundations, joyful learning
props.html:
Moriah follows the Andhra Pradesh State Board curriculum in English medium from Pre-KG to Class 10. Lessons build solid foundations in reading, writing and mathematics, and grow into science, social studies and languages in the higher classes.

Our teaching is increasingly hands-on and activity-based, in line with the National Education Policy 2020.

items.title: Early years (Pre-KG – UKG)
items.text: Play-based learning in our Early Childhood Education Center: blocks, puzzles, music, pretend play, art and early literacy and numeracy.

items.title: Primary (Classes 1 – 5)
items.text: Confident reading and writing in English and Telugu, number sense, environmental studies and plenty of activities.

items.title: High school (Classes 6 – 10)
items.text: Mathematics, sciences, social studies and languages, with careful preparation for the Class 10 State Board examinations.

items.title: English programme
items.text: Phonics, reading and spoken English with support from mentor teachers.

items.title: Science & STEM
items.text: Practical experiments, microscopes and simple robotics.

items.title: Arts & dance
items.text: Drawing, painting, music and dance, including ballet workshops.

items.title: Games & sport
items.text: Outdoor games and sport that build teamwork.

props.html:
Documents required

  • Birth certificate of the child
  • Aadhaar card of the child and parent / guardian (if available)
  • Transfer certificate and previous report card (Class 1 and above)
  • Two recent passport-size photographs

Fees and financial aid

Moriah charges tuition on a sliding-scale basis according to what each family can afford. Financial aid for qualified students is funded by our supporters, so that no child is turned away for lack of means. Please speak to the school office about your situation.

props.heading: Caring, committed and always learning
props.html:
Moriah School is led by Head Master Adam Kondru, supported by around 15 teachers and staff. They work from about 8:30 a.m. to 6 p.m., Monday to Saturday, and put in extra effort so that every student is ready for the demanding board examinations.

Our teachers know every child personally and take part in regular training — including workshops on early childhood education, play-based learning and English teaching.

news.title: Early Childhood Education Center equipped and open
news.summary: Eight classrooms full of blocks, puzzles, pretend kitchens, costumes and art corners — our youngest learners now learn through play.
news.bodyHtml:
Today if you visit the Early Childhood Education Center, you will see children playing in eight different rooms — building with many kinds of blocks, pretend cooking with pots and pans, setting tables, role-playing with costumes, painting and drawing.

This new approach is built on a simple idea: children learn best by playing and following their own curiosity, by solving real problems — how to balance and stack blocks, how to use a zipper, how to put together a puzzle — and by making mistakes and trying again.

Three visiting educators spent five days at Moriah preparing the classrooms and training our teachers, and weekly collaboration continues with our early childhood coordinator.

news.title: Enrolment reaches 250 students
news.summary: Moriah begins the school year with 250 students across three buildings.
news.bodyHtml: Enrolment at Moriah School has reached 250 students. Classrooms are now spread across three buildings to accommodate the growing number of families choosing Moriah.

news.title: Teachers complete early childhood training
news.summary: Moriah teachers took part in a five-day workshop on play-based early childhood education.
news.bodyHtml: Visiting educators worked alongside our teachers for five days, preparing classrooms and training staff in new, play-based teaching methods — with plenty of laughter and Telugu translation along the way.

news.title: Three weeks of ballet at Moriah
news.summary: A visiting ballet teacher spent three weeks teaching dance to Moriah children.
news.bodyHtml: Our children enjoyed three wonderful weeks of ballet classes with a visiting dance teacher. Students learned positions, stretches and short routines — and performed with great joy for the whole school.

news.title: A fresh coat of paint for our classrooms
news.summary: Newly painted classrooms and murals give the school a bright new look.
news.bodyHtml: Thanks to generous donors, classrooms and walls across the school were repainted, and instructional murals now brighten the corridors. Families tell us the cheerful new look is one of the reasons enrolment has grown.

seo.metaDescription: Meet the founders and leaders of Moriah School and Moriah Home in Guntur: Mrs. Devakaruna Dasari, Rev. Dasari Bhushana Rao, Bishop G. Shalem Raju and the Dasari family trustees.

props.heading: The people behind Moriah
props.subheading: A founder's vision, a church's care and a family's commitment have kept Moriah serving Guntur's children for more than 25 years.

props.heading: Mrs. Devakaruna Dasari
props.html:
Mrs. Devakaruna Dasari began her working life as a teacher. Having been given a good education as a young girl, she wanted the same for children whose families could not afford it — and in 1999 she opened Moriah School in Guntur.

She guided both the school and Moriah Home until her death in 2011. Her belief that every child can learn, and that education should lead to serving others, still shapes daily life at Moriah.

props.heading: Rev. Dasari Bhushana Rao
props.html:
Rev. Dasari Bhushana Rao founded the Bible Faith Lutheran Church of India (BFLC India) in 1978. The church he built is responsible for the direction and care of Moriah Home, and it continues to stand behind the children of Moriah today.

A memorial at Moriah honours his life of service.

props.heading: Bishop G. Shalem Raju & Mrs. Swarupa
props.html:
The Rt. Rev. G. Shalem Raju, B.A., B.D., is the Bishop of BFLC India. He directs and oversees the management of both Moriah School and Moriah Home.

His wife, Mrs. Swarupa, and their three daughters — Hepsi, Beulah and Keziah — work alongside more than 20 staff members to care for the children and support the school.

props.heading: Our trustees
props.intro: Rev. and Mrs. Dasari's three children serve as trustees, dedicated to the continuation of the church's ministry, Moriah School and Moriah Home.

props.heading: A safe, loving home for the children in our care
props.subheading: Since 1985, Moriah Home has given children who have lost one or both parents a stable home, good food and the chance to learn.

props.html:
About the home

Moriah Home provides full-time care for more than 20 children. Each of them has lost one or both parents, or needs reliable care and safe living conditions that would not otherwise be available to them. Over the years, hundreds of children have grown up here.

Every child who lives at Moriah Home attends Moriah School. Together, the home and the school give children the stability, education and encouragement they need to build a good future.

Moriah Home is under the direction and care of the Bible Faith Lutheran Church of India, and is overseen day to day by Bishop G. Shalem Raju and Mrs. Swarupa.

items.title: A safe place to live
items.text: Clean dormitories and caring adults around the clock.

items.title: Nourishing meals
items.text: Fresh food cooked every day in the home's own kitchen.

items.title: School every day
items.text: Every child studies at Moriah School, with help at homework time.

items.title: Health and play
items.text: Regular health checks, including eye exams, plus sports, dance and games.

props.html: To protect the children in our care, we do not publish their names or personal stories online.
